### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **2** package(s): `@objectstack/metadata-protocol`, `@objectstack/rest`, touching **8** documentable anchor(s).

**21** hand-written doc(s) name something this change touched — list omitted above 15 rows. Re-derive on the tree named below: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 77e993ea29f1a96126f46a5e3748847ce5eb5dd3`.

⛔ **9** release-owned page(s) also affected — read-only, see AGENTS.md Documentation Guardrails.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- the SDK route bridge reached **58** of **210** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **152** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **152**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **55** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **97** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **26** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 77e993ea29f1a96126f46a5e3748847ce5eb5dd3` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `e2aeeee07e6ce653b3ba10327c09b1e96654ec90` — the merge of head `59ef3dbe1e68f9765be5d7f503107bb7b8d91b60` into base `77e993ea29f1a96126f46a5e3748847ce5eb5dd3`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin e2aeeee07e6ce653b3ba10327c09b1e96654ec90 && git checkout e2aeeee07e6ce653b3ba10327c09b1e96654ec90
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 77e993ea29f1a96126f46a5e3748847ce5eb5dd3 59ef3dbe1e68f9765be5d7f503107bb7b8d91b60 && git checkout -B drift-repro 77e993ea29f1a96126f46a5e3748847ce5eb5dd3 && git merge --no-ff 59ef3dbe1e68f9765be5d7f503107bb7b8d91b60

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 77e993ea29f1a96126f46a5e3748847ce5eb5dd3
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs 77e993ea29f1a96126f46a5e3748847ce5eb5dd3` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

Local-runs: none
Scope: packages/rest/src/meta-collection-routes.ts, packages/metadata-protocol/src/protocol-meta-diagnostics.ts, packages/rest/src/rest-meta-diagnostics-unknown-params.test.ts, packages/rest/src/rest-server-meta-read-org-scope.test.ts, packages/metadata-protocol/src/protocol.diagnostics-store-outage.test.ts, scripts/engine-double-contract.pinned.json + packages/rest/src/meta-item-read-gate.ts (`refuseUnknownMetaListType`, `metaTypeIsLive`), packages/rest/src/error-response.ts (`handleRouteError`, `resolveErrorResponse`, `classifiedRefusalAnswer`, `nestedRefusalEnvelope`), packages/rest/src/query-multiplicity.ts (`refuseRepeatedQueryParams`), packages/rest/src/rest-server.ts (`metaItemPackageBinding`, the route host), packages/rest/src/sharing-routes.ts (`respondSharingError`), packages/metadata-protocol/src/protocol.ts (`canonicalizeMetaRequestType`, the `package` arm of `getMetaItems`, the `getMetaDiagnostics` host), packages/spec/src/meta-spelling/metadata-url-spelling.ts (`canonicalMetaUrlType`, `unrecognisedMetaTypeRefusal`), packages/types/src/data-error-classification.ts (`truncateClientMessage`, `withoutDeclaredCodePrefix`), packages/client/src/index.ts (`getDiagnostics`, `unwrapResponse`), ui/packages/data-objectstack/src/metadata-client.ts (`diagnostics`, `parseError`), ui/packages/app-shell/src/views/metadata-admin/useMetadata.ts, packages/runtime/src/domains (no diagnostics door), scripts/check-route-envelope.mjs, scripts/check-engine-double-contract.mjs, scripts/check-adr-0087-registration.mjs, docs/adr/0112-error-code-vocabulary-and-ledger.md, content/docs/deployment/validating-metadata.mdx

Read-only: the net diff `origin/main...pr27620` (7 files, +325/−5, merge-base `1ed33609`), card #27514 with all three comments (triage 6495152725, claim 6497909499, os-dev-report 6500171775), the PR body and file list, and the head's check-runs. Every cited file was read at the head's tree (`git show pr27620:…`), never from the PR body's account.

Review act: 2026-10-29T15:21Z

### ① Derived judgments

Accept-set and public-surface changes the diff implies, each judged against the cited code:

1. **`?severity=` outside `error`/`warning` → 400 `INVALID_REQUEST`; empty keeps the default.** Right. The sweep has exactly two severities (`includeWarnings = request.severity === 'warning'`, nothing else is read), so any other value was silently the error sweep. Both known callers already type the parameter as the two values (SDK `getDiagnostics` `severity?: 'error' | 'warning'`; Studio `MetadataDiagnosticsOptions.severity` the same, and `useGlobalDiagnostics` defaults it to `'error'`). The empty-string arm (`|| 'error'`) mirrors the existing empty-`type` arm (`|| undefined`) two lines down. The check runs after `refuseRepeatedQueryParams`, so the array arm never reaches it.

2. **`?type=` naming no metadata type → 400 `INVALID_REQUEST`, by `refuseUnknownMetaListType`, asked after the sweep.** Right. Read in `meta-item-read-gate.ts`: static verdict (`unrecognisedMetaTypeRefusal` returns null for every key of `META_URL_TO_SINGULAR` and every `CANONICAL_META_TYPES` member, so an alias or a canonical spelling is silent), then the live set (`metaTypeIsLive` reads `getMetaTypes`, folds both sides through `canonicalMetaUrlType`, fails open on an unreadable listing). This is byte-for-byte the verdict `GET /meta/:type` asks at line 632 of the same module, so the two doors cannot disagree on which names are types, and a plugin type the deployment carries live still answers (pinned by the new `zzz_plugin_kind` case). Asking it after the sweep is correct: `canonicalizeMetaRequestType` inside `getMetaItems` throws the #8924 near-miss refusal (status 400, code `INVALID_REQUEST`, message naming both accepted spellings) and the sweep rethrows any status-400 error, so `?type=viewes` keeps the teaching message; asked first, the static verdict would have refused `viewes` with the generic sentence. The cost is one empty listing read per refused request. Note, not a finding: the protocol-level `getMetaDiagnostics({ type: 'fieldz' })` still answers its benign count-0 (its own #8421 pin at head asserts so); the refusal lives at the door, which is the card's reach ("measured at the public diagnostics door"), and the REST route is the only transport — `packages/runtime/src/domains` has no diagnostics door.

3. **`?package=` naming a package that is not installed and that no swept item is bound to → 400 `INVALID_REQUEST`.** Right. `packageIsInstalled` reads `getMetaItems({ type: 'package' })` and matches `manifest.id ?? id`, which is exactly the shape the `package` arm of `getMetaItems` publishes (`manifestId = pkg.manifest.id`, else `pkg.id`). The order of the two halves is the right one: rows bound to an uninstalled package are real and this sweep is how an author finds them (pinned by `com.example.gone`), an installed package with no items keeps its zeros (pinned by `com.example.empty`), `package=all` folds to `undefined` through `metaItemPackageBinding` and is never checked. A disabled package is still listed under type `package` (the `isItemOfDisabledPackage` filter is skipped for that type), so it is not refused — correct, it exists. Fail-open on an unreadable listing mirrors `metaTypeIsLive` and is the right direction for an existence claim.

4. **An alias `?type=` is swept and keyed under its canonical type.** Right. `canonicalMetaUrlType` is a pure table fold (`META_URL_TO_SINGULAR[type] ?? type`), so `viewes` and `fieldz` pass through unchanged and the #8924 refusal still sees what the caller wrote. Keying `stats` and `entries` by the canonical name also hands the canonical type to `shippingPackagesOf`, `artifactLockLayerAt`, `isArtifactBacked`, `servedLockState` and `computeMetadataDiagnostics`, which previously received the raw plural — the new pin `alias.body` equals `canonical.body` is what proves the alias request now answers what the canonical one answers. Studio never sends `type` and reads `stats` with `Object.entries`, so it sees only the new key; the SDK passes `type` through and returns the body. The retired alias key is stated in the changeset.

5. **The route's existing 400 `INVALID_REQUEST` answers move from the flat `{ error: '…', code }` to the nested `{ error: { code, message } }`.** The point I was asked to break hardest. Judged in scope and right, and declared:
   - *Within triage 6495152725 ("use the route's one error envelope")*: before this PR the route hand-built two refusals, both nested — the 501 `NOT_IMPLEMENTED` and the #6877 repeated-parameter `VALIDATION_ERROR` — and the #8924 refusal alone left flat through `handleRouteError`. The nested shape is the route's own envelope; the change moves the one outlier onto it.
   - *Within ADR-0112*: D5 names `error.code` as the one end-state location; the #4007 amendment records the client reading "the two live envelopes' declared spots (flat top-level `code`, wrapped `error.code`)"; the #9232 amendment assigns envelope-position convergence to the `check:route-envelope` ratchet. That ratchet holds `meta-collection-routes.ts` at `stringError: 0`, `siblingCode: 0` (dialectOnly). A nested body is neither dialect, so the gate is quiet and the move is in the ratchet's own direction, not against it.
   - *Who reads the old shape today*: the SDK's `unwrapResponse` reads `asSemanticCode(errorBody.code) ?? asSemanticCode(errorBody.error.code)`; Studio's `parseError` reads `details.code ?? errNode.code ?? bodyObj.code` and the message off the object or the string. Both tolerate either shape. No REST test at head pins the flat shape on this route's 400s (grep over `packages/rest/src/*.test.ts`); the #8924 pins in `protocol.diagnostics-store-outage.test.ts` are protocol-level (the thrown error's `status`/`code`) and are untouched. CLI, services and plugins have no reader of the route.
   - *Classification*: it is a wire-shape change to an existing answer, so it is breaking for any consumer branching on top-level `code` for that one refusal; it is also a narrowing of the same door in the same PR. The changeset carries it under a `Clause-②: no (narrowing)` BREAKING declaration and says the old shape in its own words ("The near-miss type refusal used to answer `{ error: '…', code }`"). That is the right place and the right level (see ②). Not out of scope.
   - *Reach of the predicate*: `isDiagnosticsRefusal` is by status and code, not by origin, so any 400 `INVALID_REQUEST` thrown inside the `try` (a refusal from `resolveProtocol` included) also leaves nested. That is "one envelope" read literally and is consistent with the stated intent; recorded so the next reader does not take the docblock's four named producers as a closed list.

6. **Message bytes across the two envelopes.** Checked, because the hand-built writer bypasses `resolveErrorResponse`: that door's 4xx arm applies `withoutDeclaredCodePrefix` (anchored to `INVALID_REQUEST:` followed by a colon — none of the four producers' messages open so) and `truncateClientMessage`, which the new writer applies too. So for the producers that exist today the nested `message` is the same sentence the flat `error` carried, including the `[invalid_request]` tag `refuseUnknownMetaListType` prefixes (neither door strips it). No wire regression on the message.

7. **No new error code, no `packages/spec` change, no authorable key.** Right; both codes (`INVALID_REQUEST`, `VALIDATION_ERROR`) are ledgered members.

### ② Semver level

- Changeset `.changeset/27514-diagnostics-unknown-params.md`: `@objectstack/rest: patch`, `@objectstack/metadata-protocol: patch` — the two packages the diff moves (`packages/types`, `packages/spec`, `packages/client` and `ui/` are read, not changed). Matches.
- `Clause-②: no (narrowing)` on the PR body and the changeset body: the diff narrows the accept-set of a public REST door (three query values refused, one response key moved); the arm is the right one. This is the face that owes this record. Matches.
- `Metadata-protocol: none`: query values of a read door are not something a metadata author writes; no key, accepted value, metadata type, meaning or default changes. Matches; `none` takes `patch`, and a non-protocol breaking change ships `patch` with its BREAKING declaration and ADR-0087 disposition, which this changeset carries: `adr-0087: not-required (no-migration-prescription)`. The disposition is honest against the gate's own rule (read in `check-adr-0087-registration.mjs`): the body carries no FROM → TO prescription in arrow or table form; the remedy is the caller's query string, and no stored metadata holds a diagnostics request or response.
- `Check Changeset` on the head: success.

### ③ Boundary flags

The os-dev-report (6500171775) declares `open_questions: []`. Its four `out_of_scope_findings` and the one dev flag in the PR body, each answered:

1. **Docs follow-up owed (`content/docs/deployment/validating-metadata.mdx`).** Read at head: the query table states `severity` as `error`/`warning`, `type` as one metadata type, `package` as one package — nothing it says becomes false; it does not state the three refusals or the canonical `stats` key. A docs-only follow-up, outside this card's file surface and outside this record's scope; it does not block. Carrier: the seat, as the dev named.
2. **`scripts/engine-double-contract.pinned.json` outside the claimed surface.** Answered: the row is the gate's own `--write` output for the new rig's `findOne` double, whose body calls `assertEngineFindOnePredicate(object, query)` — the gate's declared `pinCall`; the ledger's header forbids hand-editing it. The gate carrying it (`Lint · CI, release & engine gates`) is success on the head. Accepted as part of the test, not a widening.
3. **`?type=X&package=P` reads the swept type only.** Answered: honest — the scoped sweep found nothing bound to P under X and P is not installed; the refusal text names the remedy (omit `package`, or `package=all`). Without the filter the full sweep finds the orphan rows (pinned). Not a finding.
4. **Process deviations (lint run anyway; the PR header's attribution block links the card thread).** No code effect; the PR body carries the seat's session footer. Noted, not escalated.
5. **Branch name `claude/project-thread-nx5qkr`, not `claude/issue-27514-…`.** The claim (6497909499) records it as the identity; the PR body carries `Fixes #27514`; the Duplicate Fix Guard is advisory. Not escalated.

Two flags of my own, neither a blocker:

6. **This route declares no closed query-parameter set** (no `refuseUnknownQueryParams` in the handler): `?typ=view` still answers the full sweep at 200. Pre-existing, and AGENTS.md's Route & surface ownership rule 5 converts existing routes per lane, never as one sweep, so it is not this card's — but it is the same false-all-clear class the card is about, one axis over (parameter names, not values). Should-file as its own card for the server lane.
7. **Governed surfaces:** none on the file list; `Governed Surface Queue Guard` is success on the head. The record is owed by the narrowing face alone.

### ④ Design judgment

Check-runs on the head, read at 2026-10-29T15:18Z: 48 runs, 34 success, 14 skipped, none failed, none in progress. The ten required contexts: `Build Core` success; `Governed Surface Queue Guard` success; `Test Core` and all eight shards success; the `Lint ·` and `Type Check ·` lanes (seven and four) all success; `Test UI` success; `Lint UI`, `Type Check UI`, `Build & E2E UI`, `Live E2E UI` skipped by the path filter (no `ui/` path on the diff). `Check Changeset`, `Dogfood Regression Gate` and the PR-body guards success. Those conclusions are the gate verdicts; nothing was built, run or re-run here.

**`packages/rest/src/meta-collection-routes.ts` — holds.** Read against the handler as registered, the route host (`rest-server.ts` binds `refuseUnknownMetaListType` on the host, already used by the list route), `handleRouteError`, `refuseRepeatedQueryParams` and the route-envelope ratchet. The order inside the `try` is right: protocol resolution and the 501, the arity gate, the severity check, the sweep, the type verdict, then `res.json`. The `catch` keeps `handleRouteError` for everything that is not a classified 400 `INVALID_REQUEST`, so the #8855 503 and every fault still take the shared door. One finding:
- **should-fix** — the refusal writer is hand-rolled (`isDiagnosticsRefusal` plus a literal body) where this package already has the shared derivation the sharing, security and approvals families use for exactly this re-dress: `classifiedRefusalAnswer(error)` → `nestedRefusalEnvelope(...)` (`respondSharingError` in `sharing-routes.ts` is the reference). Today the bytes are identical for the four producers (none declares `userMessage` or an unregistered code, none opens with `INVALID_REQUEST:`), so this is not a defect; but the literal writer will not pick up a future shared-classification rule (`declaredCode`, `userMessage`, prefix stripping) that every other nested family inherits, and it is a second opinion at the one boundary `error-response.ts` argues should have one. Converting it is a few lines and no behaviour change on this diff.

**`packages/metadata-protocol/src/protocol-meta-diagnostics.ts` — holds.** Read against `canonicalizeMetaRequestType`, the `package` arm of `getMetaItems`, `canonicalMetaUrlType` and the host `Pick`. The canonical fold is applied once at the top and reaches every per-type helper; the #8855/#8924 rethrow arms are untouched; the package refusal runs after the loop so an outage (503) or a near-miss (400) still wins first; `packageIsInstalled`'s `this`-less signature takes the narrower `Pick` and the host already carries `getMetaItems`. On the read-invention rule: the `catch` returns the non-refusal ("cannot disprove"), not an invented empty answer, and the read is a protocol method, not a storage seam in that rule's vocabulary — the gate lanes are success on the head. `protocol.ts` is untouched, as the PR says and the diff shows.

**`packages/rest/src/rest-meta-diagnostics-unknown-params.test.ts` — holds.** A real `ObjectStackProtocolImplementation` over a real `SchemaRegistry`, the real registered handler, both halves pinned per refusal (status plus nested `body.error.code`) and per preservation (the count or `scannedItems`, never a bare 200). The severity refusal's "service never called" half holds by construction (it throws before `getMetaDiagnostics`). The `findOne` double opens with `assertEngineFindOnePredicate`, matching its ledger row. Imports resolve to declared dependencies (`@objectstack/metadata-protocol`, `@objectstack/objectql` as devDependencies, `@objectstack/metadata-core` as a dependency of `packages/rest`).

**`packages/rest/src/rest-server-meta-read-org-scope.test.ts`, `packages/metadata-protocol/src/protocol.diagnostics-store-outage.test.ts` — hold.** Each moved pin is the alias key the card retires (`stats.views` → `stats.view`, `stats.fields` → `stats.field`), each now also asserts the alias key is absent or the key set is exactly the canonical one; nothing else in either file moves.

**`scripts/engine-double-contract.pinned.json` — holds.** One `--write` row for the new test's `findOne` double, `pinned: 1`, in the file's sorted position.

**The narrowing against the published spec on `main`:** it takes no declared capability away at any consumer — the SDK and Studio types already describe the narrowed accept-set — and it makes the door's own refusal real where it answered a silent all-clear. No must-fix.
